status: SEED — THRESHOLDS UNCHANGED AND STILL GUESSES. v0.6 makes VENTURE and PRACTICE mutually exclusive with a stated tiebreak, tightens both excludes against senior studios and capstones that v0.5 misfiled, and adds a COMPOSITION taxonomy: twelve exhaustive one-per-course buckets over the whole art unit, so a dean sees what the curriculum is made of and not only how much of it the index cares about. Requires a new classifier path for composition; the axis prompt signature also changes.
measures: What a school's catalog offers. Not what a graduate leaves with, and not what is required — see limitations.
limitations: OFFERED, NOT REQUIRED. harvest.py reads course descriptions, not degree requirement sheets, so nothing here can distinguish a required professional-practice course from an elective nobody takes. The Venture axis in particular means much less without it. Either harvest program pages, or state plainly that edition one measures offering.

Denominator is the whole catalog, not the art catalog. A large public university dilutes: 40 art-business courses among 6,000 total scores lower than 10 among 400. Normalizing by CIP-50-relevant courses rather than all courses is unresolved.
Thresholds below are placeholders. They must be set from the observed distribution once enough schools are scored, and the rule used must be published.

technology.name: Art Technology Adoption
technology.question: Does this course teach making with computational or emerging tools — AI, code, generative systems, immersive media, digital fabrication — or teach a specific software or hardware toolset for creative work?
includes: AI readiness, generative tools, machine learning as material
creative coding, computational and algorithmic making
immersive, XR, game engines, virtual production
digital fabrication, CNC, 3D printing, physical computing
named software or hardware toolsets taught for creative work
excludes: computer science, data science or engineering outside an art or design subject
art history or theory that discusses technology without making
technical trade production where the tool is the trade — audio plugin development, architectural lighting

venture.name: Art Venture and Enterprise
venture.question: Does this course teach building an enterprise around your own creative work — business formation, revenue, pricing, funding, self-employment, running a studio as a business? The test is whether the student is taught to build something of their own, not to operate inside someone else's apparatus.
includes: business formation, business models, startup and studio-as-business
pricing, revenue, contracts and negotiation for one's own work
self-employment, freelancing as an enterprise, financial management for artists
grant writing and fundraising to finance one's own practice
intellectual property, licensing and royalties as revenue
excludes: portfolio, interviewing, resume, submission preparation — PRACTICE
gallery submission, residency application, competition entry — PRACTICE
professional licensure, accreditation, internship placement — PRACTICE
SENIOR STUDIO, capstone, degree project, thesis studio — these are STUDIO, even when the description mentions professional context
medium and technique courses that mention industry or clients in passing — IMAGE DESIGN, ILLUSTRATING FOR SURFACE & PATTERN DESIGN are illustration courses
entrepreneurship taught outside art and design — The Entrepreneurial Bioengineer
accounting, finance or management taught for business students
arts administration training administrators rather than artists

practice.name: Professional Practice and Readiness
practice.question: Does this course teach operating inside an existing professional apparatus — portfolio, interviewing, submission, licensure, and the craft of curating, exhibiting or publishing? This is the control axis: it is what nearly every program already teaches, and it is what venture is usually mistaken for.
includes: portfolio development, portfolio review, artist statement as submission material
interviewing, job search, career preparation for employment
gallery, residency, competition and grant SUBMISSION mechanics
how to curate, how to exhibit, how to publish — the craft of these
professional licensure, accreditation, industry-standard practice
excludes: building an enterprise around one's own work — VENTURE
reaching people directly with one's own work — AUDIENCE
SENIOR STUDIO, senior seminar in a medium, capstone, degree project, thesis studio — these are STUDIO. Senior Photography and Senior Sculpture are studio courses, not professional readiness
studio and technique courses that mention portfolio or industry in passing — Functional Design for High-Performance Eyewear is a design course
art history and curatorial theory — that is HISTORY unless the course teaches the craft of curating as professional work

self.name: Creative Self-Development Science
self.question: Does this course teach creative process, creative development, or the person making the work as its subject — how ideas form, how a practice is navigated and sustained, how a creative life is designed?
includes: creativity science, creative cognition, psychology of creativity
creative process and ideation taught as transferable method
personal and artistic development, artistic identity and voice
life design for artists, sustaining a practice, artist wellbeing and burnout
contemplative, somatic and embodiment practice taught as creative method
critique taught explicitly as a method
excludes: ANY studio, media or technique course where making is the content
thesis or capstone whose subject is the student's own project — BUT a seminar that explicitly teaches how ideas form or how a practice is navigated DOES count
courses that merely use the words creative or creativity in describing studio work
performance and somatic training taught for performance rather than as creative method

audience.name: Audience and Distribution
audience.question: Does this course teach connecting your own work to people — marketing, sales, social media, storytelling for reach, self-distribution, building a following? The vehicle does not matter; the subject is reaching an audience directly.
includes: marketing and sales for artists and designers
social media, online presence, content and platform strategy
storytelling and narrative deployed to reach an audience
self-publishing, self-distribution, direct-to-audience channels
audience development, community and public engagement with one's own work
curating, exhibiting or publishing WHEN the subject is connecting work to people
excludes: HOW TO curate, exhibit or publish as a craft — that is PRACTICE
art history, survey and museum studies
rhetoric and composition treating audience as a writing concept
research methods mentioning published research or documentation of findings
statistics and science using distribution in its technical sense

prefilter.note: Stage one is tuned for RECALL, not precision. Over-matching is fine and expected; stage two removes the false positives. Under-matching is invisible and unrecoverable, so err wide.

classifier.note: Temperature 0 and a cached result per course-text hash, so a rerun reproduces exactly. Every classification is logged with the model and rubric version.
classifier.instruction:
For each course decide which categories, if any, it belongs to. The default is none: most courses in a university catalog belong to no category, and an empty array is the expected answer.

Apply one test per category. Would a student describing this course to a friend name the category's subject as what the course is ABOUT? If the category's subject is instead the medium, the tool, the setting, or one component of a studio course, the answer is no.

Judge what the course teaches, not what words appear in it. A ceramics course that develops the student's creative process is a ceramics course. A painting course that mentions selling work is a painting course. A statistics course using the word distribution is a statistics course. When a course is genuinely borderline, exclude it — a missing true positive costs one course; a false positive is published as evidence.

The exclusions describe subjects, not course types. Never reject a course because its title contains thesis, seminar, capstone, studio or workshop; reject it because what it teaches is the student's own project, a medium, or a technique. A course named 'Thesis Seminar: Navigating the Creative Process' teaches creative process and counts.

matching.rule: Each term is compiled with word boundaries. A trailing * means prefix match: 'negotiat*' matches negotiate, negotiating, negotiation.
matching.why: v0.1 stripped whitespace off every term before escaping it, so ' ai ' compiled to a bare substring 'ai' and matched painting, detail, available, maintain, chair. 'unity' matched community. 'tax' matched taxonomy. 'contract' matched contraction. On an art catalog the technology axis matched close to everything, which makes the shortlist rate useless as a diagnostic.

flagged_for_author.note: Not changed in v0.2 — each is an editorial call, not a mechanical repair. Run lexprobe.py and decide from the counts and samples.

probably_dead_phrases.why: No registrar writes these. A dead term cannot lower a score, only fail to raise one — so the Self axis scoring near zero would be manufactured by the lexicon rather than found in the world. That is the index's strongest sentence and it must not be an artifact.

high_carry_boilerplate.why: Catalog boilerplate ('prepares students for careers in...', 'satisfies the general education distribution requirement', 'unity of composition'). Stage two rejects them correctly, but if one term carries >40% of an axis's shortlist the axis is measuring that word. Check carry% in lexprobe before spending on stage two.

v0_4_note.hypothesis: Sonnet was not over-rejecting Self; it was executing a badly written exclude literally. Haiku ignored the same exclude, which masked the error.
v0_4_note.test: Re-run RISD alone against v0.4 on Sonnet. If ARCH 2196 returns as a Self match and the drawing and sketchbook studios stay out, the hypothesis holds and Sonnet is the better instrument precisely because it follows the rubric.
v0_4_note.if_it_holds: RISD Self = 1. One course teaching creative process as method at one of the strongest art schools in the country is the finding, not a miss.

structure.note: Technology and audience are sub-aspects of venture, not peers of it: both are capacities a venture needs. So the five axes are NOT orthogonal and MUST NOT be averaged into a composite — doing so double-counts venture. Report five separate percentages. A course may carry more than one axis (sales for artists is venture and audience), so per-school percentages may sum above 100% and that is correct.

denominator.rule: n_matched / n_art_courses — the school's own art unit, never the whole catalog
denominator.why: The question is what fraction of an art unit's offerings sit on each axis. Whole-catalog share answers a different question nobody asked. A 400-course art unit at 60% venture beats a 400-course art unit at 30% venture regardless of what else the parent university offers.
denominator.known_limitation: The art-subject set moves a median 10.6% between classifier models. This is stated, and reduced by improving the subject classifier — not a reason to use a denominator that answers a different question.

subsets.venture.entrepreneurship_explicit: flag venture matches whose TITLE contains entrepreneur/entrepreneurship, reported as a named subset count alongside the venture percentage

axis_exclusivity.rule: VENTURE and PRACTICE are mutually exclusive. A course carries at most one.
axis_exclusivity.why: They are a split of one thing — what the student is taught to depend on. Allowing both double-counted roughly 30% of venture matches in v0.5: RISD FD 2582, GRAD 144G, ILLUS 4012; MassArt EDID 230, MPFV 327; Temple ART 4096, ART 4097.
axis_exclusivity.tiebreak: If a course teaches both — a professional-practice course with a business module — assign VENTURE only when building one's own enterprise is the course's larger part. Otherwise PRACTICE. When genuinely balanced, choose PRACTICE: it is the more common and less flattering reading, and the index should not overstate venture.
axis_exclusivity.still_multi_label: Other pairs may co-occur. Sales for artists is VENTURE and AUDIENCE. Technology and audience remain sub-aspects of venture.

composition.purpose: A second, separate classification: every course in the art unit gets exactly ONE primary bucket. Exhaustive and mutually exclusive, so the buckets sum to 100% of the art unit. This answers a dean's first question — what is my curriculum actually made of — which the five axes cannot, because they only measure the parts the index cares about and overlap by design. Report composition as a pie; report axes as five percentages alongside it.
composition.question: What is this course primarily? Choose exactly one bucket. Judge what the course teaches, not what words appear in it. When a course could sit in two, choose the one a student would name if asked what the class was about.

buckets.studio: Making in a medium or technique — painting, ceramics, typography, animation, photography, industrial design studio. The core of an art curriculum.
buckets.history_theory: Art and design history, visual culture, theory, criticism, curatorial and museum studies as scholarship.
buckets.liberal_arts: Writing, literature, philosophy, science, mathematics, language, social science — non-art coursework offered inside or required by the art unit.
buckets.practice: Professional readiness: portfolio, interviewing, submission, licensure, internship preparation, the craft of curating or exhibiting as a job.
buckets.venture: Building an enterprise around one's own work: business formation, revenue, pricing, funding, self-employment, studio as a business.
buckets.technology: Computational and emerging tools, and named software or hardware toolsets taught for creative work.
buckets.self: Creative process, creativity science, artistic development, life design for artists, sustaining a practice.
buckets.audience: Marketing, sales, social media, storytelling for reach, self-distribution, audience development for one's own work.
buckets.capstone: Thesis, degree project, senior studio, final project, graduate seminar tied to the student's own body of work.
buckets.independent: Independent study, directed study, special topics with no fixed content, internship placements, administrative registration shells.
buckets.pedagogy: Art education and teacher preparation — training teachers rather than artists.
buckets.other: Anything that fits none of the above. If this bucket exceeds ~5% of a school, the taxonomy is wrong and should be revised rather than forced.

notes: CalArts carries 2,603 administrative shells — Independent Study, Internship and Thesis replicated once per department per level — which is 38% of its catalog. The independent bucket makes that visible instead of letting it silently dilute every percentage.
capstone is separated from studio deliberately. A senior thesis studio is not the same curricular object as a sophomore painting course, and deans reason about them differently.

The five axis percentages and the composition percentages will not agree exactly. Axes allow overlap and are measured against matched courses; composition is one-per-course and exhaustive. Both are reported, and the difference is stated rather than reconciled.
composition.scope: Runs over EVERY course in the school's art-subject set — no prefilter. The prefilter exists to keep cost down across 500k records; an art unit is a few hundred to a few thousand courses, so classifying all of them removes the prefilter as a source of error entirely for the dean-facing product.
